pr_title: Use `secret_key_base` from ENV or credentials when present locally
pr_body:
### Motivation / Background

Since 0c76f17f2dbf0d7ad90c890e6f334743cacce41f  a `tmp/local_secret.txt` is always used for `Rails.config.secret_key_base` in the test and development environments. Previously, `ENV["SECRET_KEY_BASE"]` or `Rails.application.credentials.secret_key_base` were used if present.

As the `secret_key_base` is used to generate signed IDs, it breaks Action Text attachments in development if they previously used the `secret_key_base` from ENV var or credentials. Accidentally deleting `tmp/local_secret.txt` will also break all local Action Text attachments.

The race condition in generating the local secret file, as reported in https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/53661, should be avoidable by setting `ENV["SECRET_KEY_BASE"]` or `Rails.application.credentials.secret_key_base`, but this currently doesn't work.

Fixes #53661 
Fixes #54277

### Details

When `ENV["SECRET_KEY_BASE"]` or `Rails.application.credentials.secret_key_base` is set for test or development, it should be used for the `Rails.config.secret_key_base`, instead of generating a `tmp/local_secret.txt`.

### Checklist

Before submitting the PR make sure the following are checked:

* [x] This Pull Request is related to one change. Unrelated changes should be opened in separate PRs.
* [x] Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why. If this PR fixes a related issue include it in the commit message. Ex: `[Fix #issue-number]`
* [x] Tests are added or updated if you fix a bug or add a feature.
* [x] CHANGELOG files are updated for the changed libraries if there is a behavior change or additional feature. Minor bug fixes and documentation changes should not be included.

Will this fix be released as part of Rails `7.x`, or only as part of Rails `8.x`?
@denisahearn it is backported to 7.2 as well: https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/ef5276a9dba516285ae1834dadedb727896aab40

I think there's a problem here:

In Rails 6.x and 7.0 the `tmp/development_secret.txt` file took precedence over the `secret_key_base` defined in `config/credentials.yml.enc` as the original intent of this file was for production use. I remember reading comments when this was introduced where people complained about not being able to have seperate environment based credentials, and the rationale was that `tmp/development_secret.txt` would deal with the only built-in case of needing a key to be different, and that developers could segment their keys within `config/credentials.yml.enc` by environment for certain keys if they wanted to.

Rails 7.1 has a bug or feature that reverses this concept so that if there's a `secret_key_base` in `config/credentials.yml.enc` it always takes precedence over `tmp/local_secret.txt` (as it was renamed). This of course breaks things.

Rails 7.2 and 8.0 (before this PR) reverted the behaviour back to what was experienced in 6.x and 7.0.

I think perhaps users who started out with Rails 7.1 have had their expectations broken with 7.2 and 8.0 but those of us who have been using Rails much longer have also had our expectations broken by 7.1, and soon to be 7.2 and 8.0 via this PR.

Is this change able to be reconsidered before you release it?

@p8, @rafaelfranca, what do you think about reverting this and just support loading the secret from `config/credentials/development.yml.enc` if it exists (else fall back to the text file). If `config/credentials.yml.enc` is the source then the default behaviour shouldn't change as the assumption is that these are production credentials.
It's a shame this wasn't given another look before 8.0.2 was released. Now you'll have a bunch of people who are confused as to why their ActionText asset links are suddenly broken in development.

I'm one of those people, and I'm disappointed to see that the release notes didn't even say much about it. It seems like deleting the `credentials.yml.enc` file fixed it though for me in my development environment (whether this has other side affects I'm not sure yet, I'm very new to Rails and just wanted to figure out how to make stuff work again while I'm trying to learn it...).

> I'm one of those people, and I'm disappointed to see that the release notes didn't even say much about it. It seems like deleting the `credentials.yml.enc` file fixed it though for me in my development environment (whether this has other side affects I'm not sure yet, I'm very new to Rails and just wanted to figure out how to make stuff work again while I'm trying to learn it...).

Sorry to hear that. Your best bet for now is to roll back to `8.0.1` and reinstate `credentials.yml.enc` and wait for this to be reverted hopefully. I've created a PR that allows for the best of both worlds but so far it's received little attention.

Note that you can always use multiple values for the `secret_key_base` :
```ruby
config.before_initialize do |app|
   app.message_verifiers.rotate secret_key_base: "8.0.1_secret_key_base"
   app.message_verifiers.rotate secret_key_base: "another_secret_key_base"
end
```

That's fine, but suddenly changing the behaviour of the `tmp` file and using the same `secret_key_base` in `credentials.yml.enc` for both development and production in a patch release seems to have taken things a bit too far. There should have at least been a deprecation cycle.

The change is insidious in that things just stop working without any errors raised other than say an image no longer being downloadable in ActionText or sessions being invalidated. Making everyone go through that same mental process to find their way to this issue isn't really fair I don't think.

Unfortunately Rails secrets has had quite a turbulent and poorly documented past so this was bound to happen eventually, and in fact has already happened before in Rails 7.1 as mentioned earlier.

> That's fine, but suddenly changing the behaviour of the tmp file and using the same secret_key_base in credentials.yml.enc for both development and production in a patch release ...

There where multiple issues in 7.2 that this PR tries to fix.
Rails not using the `secret_key_base` from credentials in development seems [like a bug](https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/54277#issuecomment-2598764148).

I know the single credentials file is the current Rails default, but I've always used environment specific credentials, so I haven't experienced the problems you ran into.

If you have a single credentials file for dev, test and production you are probably mixing other secrets as well, for example S3 secrets. Do you store ActiveStorage uploads in the same bucket as production? Does every developer have access to these secrets?

The `secret_key_base` is the only secret that is required for running a new app. 
So I always thought  the `tmp/local_secret.txt` was used for getting an application running locally without having to define `ENV['SECRET_KEY_BASE']` or using the credentials file. 

If we use it to override the `secret_key_base` in credentials to not mix dev and production secrets, all secrets in the credentials file should have their `tmp` file. I'm not sure that is viable.
Also, I think you should be able to remove the `tmp` dir anytime without your application breaking.
So I don't think we should be relying on that file to be persisted.

Would you mind opening a new issue that addresses the problem you ran into?
That would give it more visibility than this closed issue.

Thanks @p8, I will open a new issue. For context, this is the genesis of the encrypted secrets feature:

https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/30067#issue-247861677

In DHH's first comment he claims that the file should only be for production and that other development keys can be handled separately. Of course this wasn't too popular and it appears that multiple environment credentials were deployed via this PR:

https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/33521

You're right in that I was forced to store development secrets in that file where it made sense for them to differ (e.g. R2 storage keys). I definitely don't store development assets in my production bucket! :)

But for some other credentials it doesn't matter that they're the same. At the time I remember being frustrated at the removal of the fallback feature of the original secrets system.

I guess going forward, if nothing else is done, one needs to have an encrypted secrets file for every environment they use (including `test`) with keys repeated across those environments.

This PR is a significant breaking change for those of us with older Rails apps that have grown through all these permutations of secrets and credentials. Perhaps in the meantime you could change the 8.0.2 CHANGELOG to make it quite loud about this being a breaking change and that users need to create themselves a development encrypted credentials file and copy their tmp file `secret_key_base` across to it (in addition to all the other necessary keys in their production encrypted secrets file) in order for development to still work.

issue_context.title: Rails no longer looks for `secret_key_base` in credentials (in development)
issue_context.body:
Rails 7.1 automatically found `secret_key_base` in credentials when in development env.

Rails 7.2 doesn't look there anymore, when in development env. It now always generates a secret file and uses that.

It seems the only way to bring back credentials lookup in development is by setting it manually in development.rb:

```ruby
config.secret_key_base = credentials[:secret_key_base]
```

This change is not mentioned in Rails 7.1 -> 7.2 upgrade guide, so it was quite unsettling to find out that all my cookies stopped working after the update. (Since Rails silently switched to using the generated key over the key in my credentials file).

Here's the [relevant code](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/4666f596861a2d53ff0d7fb055206355b5a13de2/railties/lib/rails/application/configuration.rb#L511).

Whether the solution might be to document this in the upgrade guide, or make Rails honor the key stored in credentials, it seems to be an issue worth addressing.
comments: Yes. That is a bug. Mind to open a PR?
Yes, that is true. Let me fix that one

Here's what I've noticed too:

With Rails 6.1 and 7.0 in development, the `secret_key_base` is read from `tmp/development_secret.txt` as a preference over the production `secret_key_base` defined via `rails credentials:edit`. This is reversed in the latest Rails 7.1 so now it uses the production `secret_key_base` defined via `rails credentials:edit` instead of what's in `tmp/local_secret.txt`.

I've confirmed this by loading the key from the text file into the credentials and all of the ActionText attachments work again.

I've now moved my upgrading process to Rails 7.2 and can conform as of 7.2.2.1 (probably earlier) the `tmp/local_secret.txt` file takes precedence over the `secret_key_base` in `config/credentials.yml.enc` again.

Perhaps there should be a backport of this behaviour to Rails 7.1 to prevent people wasting time trying to sort it out?
